meaning: to start planning again because the previous attempt has failed
literal_translation: начать всё заново, потому что предыдущий план не сработал
example: The prototype failed every test, so the engineers had to go back to the drawing board.
origin: From design and engineering offices, where plans were drawn on boards; the exact origin is uncertain

wrong_meanings.meaning: to draw a picture on a wooden board for fun
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This takes the words literally, but the idiom describes restarting a failed plan, not making art

wrong_meanings.meaning: to hang a finished drawing on the wall of an office
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with displaying completed work

wrong_meanings.meaning: to finish a project quickly before the deadline
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which describes starting again because the earlier work did not succeed

explanation: 'Back to the drawing board' means that an idea or design has failed and must be planned again from the beginning. It is common in discussions of technology and product development.
